steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how has your skin been since we set up your home routine? I usually hear one of three things. I'm still using it, and my skin looks good. Or I ran out, or the routine slipped. Or I stopped, and my skin is back to how it was. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Using the Routine
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone sticks with their routine. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know your skin is still doing well.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

steps.title: Ran Out or the Routine Slipped
steps.content:
That happens, {{contact_first_name}}. Home routines can slip when life gets busy. There's no judgment. What made it harder to keep up?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Stopped and Skin Changed
steps.content:
I'm sorry, {{contact_first_name}}. Skin keeps changing after a routine stops. It's not anything you did wrong. What changed first?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, can I ask you a few quick questions about anything else you've noticed?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Transition: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to the routine. First, can I ask a few quick questions so your file is current?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down every concern they name. You'll recap them in a moment.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to ask about your skin and your current routine. Just let me know what applies to you.

Would you like to get your routine back on track?

Are there products you ran out of?

Have you noticed any dryness or flaking?

Are you having any breakouts?

Has your skin been looking dull?

Have you noticed sun spots or uneven tone?

Are fine lines starting to bother you?

How about redness or sensitivity?

Have you noticed large pores or rough skin?

Would you like to get your sunscreen habit back?

Have you noticed any loosening or sagging?

(Recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down every concern they name, including the first one.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to ask about your skin and your current routine. Just let me know what applies to you.

Would you like to get your routine back on track?

Are there products you ran out of?

Have you noticed any dryness or flaking?

Are you having any breakouts?

Has your skin been looking dull?

Have you noticed sun spots or uneven tone?

Are fine lines starting to bother you?

How about redness or sensitivity?

Have you noticed large pores or rough skin?

Would you like to get your sunscreen habit back?

Have you noticed any loosening or sagging?

(Recap everything, including what they mentioned first, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, between these, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask about {{main_concern}} so your file is current.

(Ask these questions in order. Pause after each.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a few weeks, or more like months?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you notice now and then, or every time you look in the mirror?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with photos, going out, or feeling put together?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that.

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Read back their three answers: how long, how often, what it gets in the way of.)

So it's been on your mind a while, and you notice it most times you look in the mirror. At its worst it gets in the way of what you mentioned. Did I get that right?

(Say what they named: photos, going out, or feeling put together. Let them answer. If they correct you, take the correction and move on.)

It sounds like you'd like your skin and routine to feel manageable again. Is that fair to say?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. If we can help, we'll walk you through the options. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Either way you'll know where you stand. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Uncover the Real Concern
steps.content:
Okay, {{contact_first_name}}. I'm not going to push you on it. What's the part giving you pause?

(Let them answer. Then tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Why Did They Stop?
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad your skin is doing well.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in for skin checks?

(Let them answer. Do not argue with it.)

Skin needs can change, even when a routine works well. A skin check helps keep your file current. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for a skin check. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m using drugstore stuff now and it’s fine”
steps.content:
That's okay, {{contact_first_name}}. There's no judgment about what's on your shelf.

Can I ask, is it doing what you want for {{main_concern}}, or just not making things worse?

(Let them answer. Do not knock what they use.)

Those are two different jobs. Drugstore products are built to be gentle enough for everyone, which is why they rarely move anything. The products here are picked for your skin and strong enough to change it. If what you're using is enough, {{provider_name}} will tell you to keep going. If it isn't, you'll find out now instead of a year from now.

Would it help to know for sure?

steps.title: Objection: “I didn’t see enough of a difference”
steps.content:
I appreciate you telling me, {{contact_first_name}}. That's worth hearing.

Can I ask, how long did you stay with the routine before you stopped?

(Let them answer. Do not promise results on the call.)

Active products work on the skin's cycle, and most need two or three months before the change is visible. Stopping at six weeks looks like nothing happened. Your notes show exactly what was done, so we're not guessing.

{{provider_name}} can look at {{main_concern}} today and hear what you were hoping for. Then you'll hear plainly whether it was the timing, the strength, or the wrong product.

Is that worth one visit to find out?

steps.title: Objection: “The routine was too many steps”
steps.content:
That's useful to know, {{contact_first_name}}, and it's the most common reason routines stop.

Can I ask, was it the morning, the evening, or both that felt like too much?

(Let them answer.)

A routine that doesn't fit your life isn't a good routine, no matter what's in it. Most of the change for {{main_concern}} comes from two or three products used every day, not seven used sometimes. {{provider_name}} can cut it down to the steps that matter and drop the rest.

Would a shorter routine be worth coming in to set up?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m not sure it’s worth it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask, is that about the cost, or about whether you'd see a change?

(Let them answer. If it's cost, use the cost answer.)

Worth it comes down to one question, and it's whether {{main_concern}} is still bothering you. If it is, it's been bothering you for a while now, and it hasn't sorted itself out. Skin doesn’t hold still while you decide. The routine is what keeps it from drifting.

{{provider_name}} can look at where things stand and tell you plainly what's realistic. If the answer is that it's not worth it for you, you'll hear that too.

Would knowing that be worth one short visit?

steps.title: If They Say: “My skin was doing fine”
steps.content:
That makes sense, {{contact_first_name}}. When skin looks good, a check can stop feeling important. Skin needs can still change over time.

Does that make sense?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they name another reason, go back and tap it.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for a skin check. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: Cost or Budget
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. A skin check is just a look. You're not committing to anything.

Does that seem fair?

(Let them answer.)

(Do not quote prices or sell products on the call.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they name another reason, go back and tap it.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “Life got busy”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up, and skin checks get pushed down the list. We can work around your schedule.

Would that work?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they name another reason, go back and tap it.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's find a time that's easy for you. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “I’ll come back if my skin acts up”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Skin needs can change before a bigger issue stands out. A check lets us see how things look now.

Does that sound right?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they name another reason, go back and tap it.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for a skin check. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: They Moved or Tried Another Provider
steps.content:
That's understandable, {{contact_first_name}}. Things change. If you're nearby, we'd be glad to see you again. Your skin history is still in your file.

Would that be okay?

(Let them answer.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they name another reason, go back and tap it.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you back on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m considering another option”
steps.content:
That's fair. Can I ask what you're looking at, like a drugstore line, a dermatologist, or another office?

(Let them answer. Do not knock the other option.)

Those can all make sense, and some people do well combining them. The part that's hard to compare from home is what would move {{main_concern}} for you. {{provider_name}} already knows how your skin responded last time, so you're not starting over here.

Come in, get a straight answer on where things stand, and then compare. If the other option turns out to be the better fit, you'll be choosing it for a reason.

Is that a fair way to decide?

steps.title: Objection: Cost
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it the cost of the skin check itself, or the thought of buying a whole set of products again?

(Let them answer. Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

This first skin check is one appointment, not a shelf of products. You'll hear what anything past that costs before you decide on it. And since you've been here before, we're not starting from scratch, and starting from scratch is the expensive part.

The other side of it is what {{main_concern}} is already costing you, the things you mentioned a minute ago. That's the part I'd hate to see keep adding up.

Can we at least get the look on the calendar?

steps.title: Objection: “I don’t have time”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it finding time for the first skin check, or the worry about a long routine again?

(Let them answer.)

Right now we're only talking about one skin check. {{provider_name}} looks at {{main_concern}} and tells you what it would take from there. Sometimes that’s two products. Sometimes it’s a short plan, and you’ll hear that up front so you can decide. Nobody is selling you a routine on the phone.

We'll fit that first skin check around your schedule, not the other way around.

Could you find a short window for that?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to talk to my spouse”
steps.content:
Of course. Is it more about the money side, or do you two just make these decisions together?

(Let them answer. If it's money, use the cost answer.)

That's fair, and I'm not asking you to commit to anything they'd need to weigh in on. Right now, all you can tell them is that {{main_concern}} is on your mind. After the skin check, you can tell them what's going on and what it would take. That's an easier conversation to have. And if they'd like to come along, they're welcome.

Can we pencil it in, and you can move it after you two talk?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Usually when someone says that, there's one specific thing on their mind. What's the part you'd want to think over?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

Okay. I'm not trying to rush you. The one thing I'd say is that {{main_concern}} is on your mind. It's been that way for a while, and it hasn't sorted itself out on its own. The skin check is how you get the information you'd be thinking with. You can think it over just as easily after you know what's going on.

Would it be easier to think it over once you have the answers?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I can do that, {{contact_first_name}}. What would you want it to cover, so I send the right thing?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

I'll be straight with you, though. Anything I send is going to be general. It can't tell you what's realistic for {{main_concern}} specifically. That takes {{provider_name}} looking at your skin, and that's one short skin check.

Let's do both. I'll send the information, and we'll put a time on the calendar. If what I send answers your question, you can call and cancel, no problem.

Does doing both work for you?
